subject: history

moments.title: First Battle of St Albans
moments.body: 22 May 1455: Richard, Duke of York, defeats Henry VI's forces at St Albans. The Duke of Somerset is killed. Henry VI — periodically incapacitated by mental illness — is captured. The first action of what becomes a 32-year dynastic war.
moments.takeaway: The roots lie earlier: Henry VI's weakness, factional politics, the loss of France in 1453 destabilising the regime.

moments.title: Towton
moments.body: 29 March 1461 (Palm Sunday): Edward IV defeats Lancastrian forces at Towton in Yorkshire. Possibly the bloodiest battle on English soil — contemporary accounts put deaths at 28,000, modern estimates lower but still in the tens of thousands.
moments.takeaway: Edward IV's reign (1461-83) was relatively stable. The wars renewed under his son Edward V and brother Richard III.

moments.title: Bosworth Field
moments.body: 22 August 1485: Henry Tudor defeats Richard III, who is killed in the fighting — the last English king to die in battle. Henry becomes Henry VII. He marries Elizabeth of York in 1486, founding the Tudor dynasty.

quote.attrib: Richard III, allegedly at Bosworth, in the Croyland Chronicle account

moments.takeaway: Richard's remains were lost until rediscovered under a Leicester car park in 2012, identified by DNA and scoliosis evidence.

now.title: Tudor mythmaking
now.body: Polydore Vergil and Thomas More wrote Tudor-era histories blackening Richard III. Shakespeare's 'Richard III' (c. 1593) cemented the image. Modern revisionism (the Richard III Society, founded 1924) has rebalanced — Richard's administrative record was competent; the Princes in the Tower remain genuinely unresolved.
now.open_questions: Did Richard kill the Princes? The case is circumstantial. Henry VII had motive too. Alison Weir, Philippa Langley and David Horspool have argued opposing positions on the same evidence.

reflection: Dynastic war is messy: shifting allegiances, no clean ideological line, generations of revenge. The Tudor narrative of unity restored after chaos is itself a piece of political work.
